summary: HfO2 films were grown using atomic layer deposition from HfCl4 and H2O on silicon substrates at temperatures ranging from 226 to 750 °C. The study focused on the effects of growth temperature on the structure, dielectric properties, and impurity content of the films. The films were analyzed for their crystalline structure, residual impurities, and dielectric behavior, with particular attention to the impact of temperature on the formation of monoclinic and other polymorphs of HfO2.
evidence: HfO2 films were atomic layer deposited from HfCl4 and H2O on Si(100) in the temperature range of 226–750 °C. The films consisted of dominantly the monoclinic polymorph. The content of residual hydrogen and chlorine monotonously decreased with increasing growth temperature. The effective permittivity insignificantly depended on the growth temperature and water partial pressure. Capacitance-voltage curves exhibited marked hysteresis especially in the films grown at 400–450 °C.
